input: # divergent.tsv — where this repo's THREE ports DISAGREE, executed.
#   input  .proto source. Escapes \n \r \t \\ are decoded, as in spec/.
#   ts,go,rust
#          what each port produces: the FileDescriptorProto as JSON, or
#          ERROR:<message fragment>.
#   why    what causes it, and where the repair lives.
# NOT A FIXTURE, and deliberately NOT under spec/: both other runtimes run
# every file in spec/ by directory listing, and these rows are expected to
# disagree. A fixture fails when behaviour REGRESSES; this fails BOTH ways,
# because when a port is repaired to agree with the others the row still
# claims they differ, so the suite goes red and names the row to delete. A
# divergence recorded as a passing test of current behaviour survives its
# own repair with nothing red, which is how the 2026-08 fleet audit found
# 29 recorded claims contradicted by execution.
# Every column is EXECUTED: ts/test/divergent.test.ts reads `ts`,
# go/divergent_test.go reads `go` and rs/tests/divergent_test.rs reads
# `rust`, each through its runtime's half of the shared Register. Until
# 2026-09-22 only `rust` ran and the other two were measured by hand; a
# recorded measurement goes stale the moment a port moves, and nothing
# says so.
# --- the TypeScript prototype-chain defect -------------------------------
# `SCALAR_TYPES[bare]` is a bare object literal indexed by text from the
# source, so a field type named after an Object.prototype member finds an
# inherited value instead of `undefined`: `__proto__` yields the prototype
# object itself (`"type":{}`), and the eleven function-valued members yield
# a function, which JSON.stringify drops, so the field loses both `type`
# and `typeName`. Go and Rust both record the `typeName` protoc's parser
# records. The repair belongs in TypeScript (a `Map`, or an own-property
# check); until it lands, Rust cannot match TypeScript here and would not
# want to.
syntax = "proto2";\nmessage M { optional __proto__ a = 1; }\n
why: TS defect: SCALAR_TYPES[name] reaches Object.prototype - repair in ts/src/build-descriptor.ts

input: # Rust agrees with the canonical TypeScript on each of these four, and Go
# does not. They are recorded here rather than in Rust's DIVERGENCE.md
# entries because the port that differs from canonical is Go.
#   1. A field option named `__proto__` is dropped by TypeScript, because
#      `map[name] = value` on a bare object with a primitive value sets the
#      prototype and creates no property. Rust drops it deliberately for
#      the same reason. A Go map keeps it. (An `option __proto__ = ...;`
#      STATEMENT is a different path in all three and survives everywhere:
#      the canonical form there is a computed-key object literal, which
#      does create an own property.)
#   2. `Number("-0x10")` is NaN: ECMA-262 allows no sign before a
#      NonDecimalIntegerLiteral, so the literal is kept as text. Go's
#      jsNumber strips the sign first and answers -16.
#   3. `Number("1_0")` is NaN: a numeric separator is a source-literal
#      feature and not part of StringToNumber, so the field number is NaN
#      and the descriptor's JSON writes null. Go's toInt answers 10.
#      (`1_0` is accepted at all only because the shared tabnas lexer is
#      more permissive than .proto here; see test/protobuf-suite.)
#   4. A proto3 `optional group` is proto3-optional in TypeScript, which
#      synthesises the `_g` oneof for it. Go's buildGroup discards the flag.
syntax = "proto3";\nmessage M { int32 a = 1 [__proto__ = 2]; }\n
why: Go defect: a field option named __proto__ survives a Go map - repair in go/build_descriptor.go
